answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after randomly sampled peers verify its outputs. A quill-like signed work log links each submission to the same stake, while a trellis of reputation limits how quickly a new identity gains influence; a nebula of fake accounts cannot multiply voting power without multiplying locked capital. The attacker therefore pays an upfront opportunity cost and risks slashing for dishonest work, making mass identities expensive rather than free.
